answer: Agents managing a citrus grove and urban garden can deter Sybil attacks using epoch-bound verifiable delay functions. Each node must compute a sequential Wesolowski proof from a public randomness beacon and anchor it to a session key before voting. Because individual proofs resist parallelization, spawning fake identities costs scarce dedicated core-time per account every epoch. However, it cannot stop wealthy adversaries from renting large CPU fleets to evaluate proofs concurrently.
